[Warm, conversational voice, measured delivery] An idea starts with one person. [pause for 0.25 seconds] Someone else needs to understand it well enough to act. [pause for 0.25 seconds] This repository turns explanations into videos, with narration and diagrams that move together.

[pause for 1.25 seconds]

Remotion turns React code, using web technologies such as HTML, CSS, and SVG, into video.

[pause for 1.25 seconds]

You can start with an essay. [pause for 0.25 seconds] An AI coding agent uses the repository's skills to shape the script, generate the voiceover, and build a video around it. [pause for 0.25 seconds] The diagrams follow the spoken explanation.

[pause for 1.25 seconds]

Or start with a recording: a podcast, an interview, or a discussion. [pause for 0.25 seconds] The original voice and sequence stay intact. [pause for 0.25 seconds] The agent maps the ideas to timed visuals, so the explanation develops as you listen.

[pause for 1.25 seconds]

Skills give the agent instructions for these tasks. [pause for 0.25 seconds] Generate video essay guides the adaptation, with generate essay audio handling narration. [pause for 0.25 seconds] Animate recorded audio guides the workflow when the recording already exists.

[pause for 1.25 seconds]

Supporting Remotion skills cover creating compositions, animation, captions, maps, and rendering. [pause for 0.25 seconds] The essay SDK supplies the reusable visual behavior, keeping each video's code focused on its content and timing.

[pause for 1.25 seconds]

Now we are testing that same toolkit on technical documentation, starting with this repository. [pause for 0.25 seconds] This video uses the existing SDK to explain what it can do. [pause for 0.25 seconds] Part two will show developers how to get started.

[pause for 1.25 seconds]

[Softening, reflective] Start with something you want to explain, and ask your AI coding agent to make a video. [pause for 0.75 seconds]
